 Acquisition Act, Against The Judgment And Award Dated
 18.08.2011, Passed In Lac No.91/2005, On The File Of The
 Senior Civil Judge At Mudhol & Etc.

 Mfa No. 102569 of 2015
 This Appeal, Coming On For Further Hearing, This Day,
The Court Delivered The Following:
 Judgment

The appellant is the claimant in LAC.No.91/2005 on the file of the learned Senior Civil Judge at Mudhol ("the Reference Court" for short), is impugning the common judgment and award dated 18.08.2011 passed along with LAC.No.83/2005 and other connected maters confirming the award of the Special Land Acquisition Officer ("the SLAO" for short) fixing the compensation for the land that was acquired at the rate of Rs.36,000/- per acre.
2.
Brief facts of the case are that, the claimant being the owner of Sy.No.53/1 measuring 1.07 acres has claimed compensation since the land in question was notified for acquisition for forming canal.
The SLAO fixed the compensation at the rate of 36,000/- per acres.
Therefore, the matter was referred to the Reference Court to determine the just compensation.
In all 10 reference was considered by the Reference Court i.e., LAC.Nos.83 to 92 of 2005.
PW.1-Basappa Kenchareddy was examined on behalf of all the claimants and got marked Exs.1 to P.40 in support of such contention.

3. The Trial Court taking into consideration these materials on record, passed the impugned judgment and award rejecting the reference of the appellant and confirming the compensation awarded by the SLAO.
4. Being aggrieved by the same, the claimant in LAC.No.91/2005 is before this Court.

5. Heard Sri Rajashekhar B.Halli, learned counsel for the appellant, Sri M.H. Patil, learned Addl.
Govt.
Advocate for respondent No.1 and Sri Shivaraj C. Bellakki, learned counsel for respondent No.2-benificiary.

6. Learned counsel for the appellant contended that the land belonging to the appellant is an agriculture land and in a similar case, the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in MFA.No.25470/2011 (LAC) vide order dated 29.07.2015, awarded compensation of Rs.2,20,000/- per acre.
Since the said appeal refers to LAC.No.88/2005 decided under the common judgment, the same compensation is to be awarded in the present case.
7. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.2- benificiary opposing the appeal submitted that there is no reason to award compensation as awarded in MFA.No.25470/2011.
He submits that, as per Ex.P.19, the record of rights pertaining to claimant, the land acquired was a dry land.

sentences.text: the Reference Court found that the lands were irrigated lands, there was enhancement of compensation.

He refers to the land in LAC.No.84/2005 as referred to by the Reference Court in paragraph No.13 of the impugned judgment, he contended that the record of rights discloses that it was an irrigated land and therefore there was enhancement of compensation.
Since it is a case of dry land, applying the principles laid down by the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in MFA.No.22810/2011, 1/3rd is to be deducted.
Accordingly he prays for passing appropriate order.
8. The contention of learned counsel for respondent No.2-beneficiary is supported by the learned Additional Government Advocate for respondent No.1.

9. Perused the material on record.
10.
Admittedly, in all 10 LAC references were made before the Reference Court and common judgment was passed determining the compensation.
It is pertinent to note that the Reference Court has bifurcated the cases on the ground that the lands acquired are either dry lands or irrigated lands.
Wherever there are dry lands, the compensation awarded by the SLAO was confirmed.
Wherever it is found that the lands are irrigated lands, the compensation was enhanced by fixing the same at Rs.1,80,000/- per acre.
However, some of the claimants have preferred appeals.

One such appeal is MFA.No.25470/2011, wherein the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court enhanced the compensation to Rs.2,20,000/- per acre taking into consideration enhancement of compensation in the connected matter i.e., MFA.No.25466/2011 which arise out of LAC.No.84/2005 under the common judgment.
The land in question in LAC No. 84/2005 is an irrigated land where sugarcane was being grown.

Therefore, it is held that the finding of the Trial Court that the claimant is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,80,000/- per acre is to be modified and accordingly appeal was allowed fixing the compensation of Rs.2,20,000/- per acre.
11. It is pertinent to note that, the LAC.No.84/2005 referred to by the Reference Court is in respect of an irrigated land.
The Record of right pertaining to the land acquired shows that it is an irrigated land having the source of water from the bore-well and the sugarcane was being grown.

However,
the said distinction was not brought to the notice of the Co- ordinate Bench of this Court and the compensation was awarded at Rs.2,20,000/- in M.F.A. No. 25470/2011.
12.

It is specifically contended in the present case that even the Record of rights relied on by the claimant discloses that the land in question is a dry land and therefore the compensation that is awarded in respect of an irrigated land cannot be awarded in the present case.
On perusal of the materials on record, the learned counsel is justified in making such submission.

13. Learned counsel for respondent No.2 placed reliance on the decision in MFA.No.22810/2011,
wherein the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court placing reliance on the decision in Land Acquisition Officer Vs. Karigowda 1 held that the market value of the dry land would be determined by reducing the compensation which was determined in respect of the wet land by 1/3rd.

sentences.text: In view of the above, I am of the opinion that the compensation that is fixed by the Co-ordinate Bench of this Court taking into consideration the lands as an irrigated land at Rs.2,20,000/- could be taken as a base in the present case.
1/3rd of the value determined for irrigated land is to be deducted, since the land in question in the present case is a dry land.
However the reference Court was not justified in confirming the award passed by the SLAO.

The claimant is entitled for enhancement of compensation as under:
Rs.2,20,000.00 - 1/3rd = Rs.1,47,000/- per acre 15.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER 1.
The appeal is allowed in part.
2. The impugned judgment and award dated 18.08.2011 passed in LAC.No.91/2005 by the Reference Court is modified.

3. It is held that the claimant-appellant is entitled for compensation at Rs.1,47,000/-
per acre along with all statutory benefits.

4. Draw the award accordingly.
5.
Send back the trial Court records along with a copy of the judgment and award.

SD/-

opennyai_summary.decision:

Rs.2,20,000.00 - 1/3rd = Rs.1,47,000/- per acre 15.

3. It is held that the claimant-appellant is entitled for compensation at Rs.1,47,000/-
